All panels are produced by
[`script/Figure6.R`](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/immgenT-GP-analysis/blob/main/script/Figure6.R).
The code below is shown for reference (not re-executed on this page); the
images are its pre-rendered output.

## Setup

Data loading and the tissue-associated GP set, shared across the panels below.

```{r fig6-setup, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", c("^", "Load data", "Shared AUC setup")), eval=FALSE}
```

### The 32 tissue-associated GPs

Panels (a) and (b) show the union of the two criteria by which a GP is called
tissue-associated: its raw mean loading reaches 0.1 in at least one of the 18
tissues (31 GPs), or its one-vs-rest tissue AUC exceeds 0.9 under the
positivity mask (7 GPs, the organ-specific set highlighted in (d) and (e)).
Six GPs satisfy both, so 32 are shown.

```{r fig6-selection, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6a/6b selection"), eval=FALSE}
```

## (a) Tissue mean loading {#fig6a}

```{r fig6a-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6a:"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6a-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6a.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6a.** Row-centered mean GP activity across 18 tissues, for the 32
tissue-associated GPs. For each GP, its mean loading across tissues is
subtracted from every tissue mean, so the color says where a program is more
or less active than its own average. Mean GP activity computed in samples at
baseline. GP37 is shown on the last row: it is strongly mammary-gland-specific
but active in few cells, so its mean loading is small at every tissue (see
(c)).
:::

## (b) Lineage mean loading {#fig6b}

```{r fig6b-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6b:"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6b-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="70%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6b.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6b.** The same 32 GPs across the 8 T cell lineages, in the row order of
(a). Mean GP activity computed in samples at baseline. Note the different
color scale: green-purple rather than blue-red, and -0.1 to 0.1 rather than
-0.2 to 0.2, since spreading a program over 8 lineages instead of 18 tissues
gives correspondingly smaller deviations.
:::

## (c) GP37+ rate in mammary gland vs. elsewhere {#fig6c}

```{r fig6c-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6c:"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6c-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="60%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6c.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6c.** Proportion of GP37-active cells in each lineage in the mammary
gland compared with all other organs (faded color bar).
:::

## (d) Max AUC: organ vs. cluster {#fig6d}

```{r fig6d-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", c("6d prep", "6d:")), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6d-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="60%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6d.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6d.** Scatterplot showing each GP's prediction (AUC) of organ of origin
(x-axis) versus level 2 cluster (y-axis). The seven organ-specific GPs are
highlighted in red, and a contrasting set of cluster-specific GPs (high
cluster AUC, low organ AUC) in blue.
:::

## (e) Organ, GP, and cluster alluvial diagram {#fig6e}

```{r fig6e-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6e:"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6e-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6e.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6e.** Alluvial plot showing how tissue-specific GP activity is
distributed across clusters. For each organ, GP-active cells are traced to
their cluster annotation. Flows are colored by GP, and width is proportional
to the number of cells.
:::
